advances: For a finite block of reflected one-dimensional reservoirs, odd-imbalance second moments and even-gap first moments give a rigorous lower bound for actual endpoint-minimum stock. A single global orientation choice converts that stock into a feasible full-occurrence canonical packing with only one factor of two. Under the stated excess-reservoir and moment hypotheses, the explicit threshold \(m\delta\ge16C(1+\log(1/\delta))^2\) pays the canonical gap-cutoff denominator. No one-dimensional price estimate or unrestricted product theorem is a premise.
author: research-agent
external_sources: None. Accepted fact `488f0a583886b5fc` supplies the canonical complete-table, potential, gap, and full-occurrence packing conventions. The probability estimate, explicit endpoint-minimum packing, and quantitative threshold are proved above using finite sums and elementary inequalities.
proof:
First, \(0\in\mathcal U_{J_i}\) and its summand in \(R_i\) is \(w^i_{J_i}>0\). Every support is finite and invariant under \(v\mapsto-v\). Interchanging the two endpoints proves the symmetry of \(Q_i\), the evenness of \(G_i\), and the oddness of \(A_i\). Log-concavity of the complete extension gives \(w^i_{J_i}\ge\sqrt{w^i_{J_i+v}w^i_{J_i-v}}\); taking logarithms gives \(G_i(v)\ge0\). All functions used in expectations are finite on their finite supports. Thus the statistics are well defined, including the case of a singleton profile. Oddness and symmetry imply \(\mathbb E_{Q_i}A_i=0\). Also \(R_i\le W_i\), since the pointwise inequality \(\sqrt{xy}\le(x+y)/2\), summed over all integer displacements with zero entries included, gives this bound.

The extension \(f(x_1,\ldots,x_m)=\prod_i f_i(x_i)\) is finite-valued and agrees with every entry of the block table, including all its zeros. Multiplying the one-dimensional log-concavity inequalities proves log-concavity of \(f\). Consequently the block table is globally extendable in the sense of `488f0a583886b5fc`, so its canonical packing definitions apply. Its positive support, total weight, maximum weight, and potential have exactly the product and sum formulas in the statement. In particular, for a nonzero displacement \(\mathbf v\in\mathcal U_{\mathbf J}\), the two distinct endpoints have midpoint \(\mathbf J\), unique coefficients \(1/2,1/2\), and canonical gap

\[
G_{\{\mathbf J+\mathbf v,\mathbf J-\mathbf v\}}
=\frac{\phi_{\mathbf J+\mathbf v}+\phi_{\mathbf J-\mathbf v}}2-\phi_{\mathbf J}
=\sum_iG_i(v_i)=G(\mathbf v).
\]

These pairs are affinely independent even if the support of the entire table is lower-dimensional. The central singleton has canonical gap zero. Thus \(L\) here is the canonical pair gap cutoff itself, without a curvature normalization factor.

Under \(Q\), the coordinates are independent. The zero means just established make every cross term vanish, so

\[
\mathbb E_Q G=g,
\qquad \mathbb E_Q A=0,
\qquad
\mathbb E_Q A^2
=\sum_i\mathbb E_{Q_i}A_i^2
+2\sum_{i<j}(\mathbb E_{Q_i}A_i)(\mathbb E_{Q_j}A_j)
=a.
\]

For each \(\mathbf v\in\mathcal U_{\mathbf J}\), the potential difference gives \(\log(w_{\mathbf J+\mathbf v}/w_{\mathbf J-\mathbf v})=-2A(\mathbf v)\). For any positive numbers \(x,y\), \(\min\{x,y\}=\sqrt{xy}\exp(-|\log(x/y)|/2)\). Therefore

\[
\begin{aligned}
\min\{w_{\mathbf J+\mathbf v},w_{\mathbf J-\mathbf v}\}
&=\left(\prod_i\sqrt{w^i_{J_i+v_i}w^i_{J_i-v_i}}\right)e^{-|A(\mathbf v)|}\\
&=\left(\prod_iR_i\right)Q(\mathbf v)e^{-|A(\mathbf v)|}.
\end{aligned}
\]

Summing proves the exact stock identity. This identity expresses the actual endpoint minimum in terms of the reflected law; it does not declare the geometric mean a capacity.

For \(L\ge0\), the event \(\{G\le L\}\) contains \(\mathbf0\), whose \(Q\)-probability is positive, so \(p_L>0\). Conditional Jensen's inequality for the convex function \(x\mapsto e^{-x}\), followed by conditional Cauchy-Schwarz, yields

\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb E_Q\!\left[e^{-|A|}\mathbf1_{\{G\le L\}}\right]
&=p_L\mathbb E_Q[e^{-|A|}\mid G\le L]\\
&\ge p_L\exp\!\left(-\mathbb E_Q[|A|\mid G\le L]\right)\\
&\ge p_L\exp\!\left(-\sqrt{\mathbb E_Q[A^2\mid G\le L]}\right)\\
&\ge p_L\exp\!\left(-\sqrt{a/p_L}\right).
\end{aligned}
\]

The last step uses \(\mathbb E_Q[A^2\mathbf1_{\{G\le L\}}]\le\mathbb E_Q A^2=a\). In particular it does not assume that conditioning preserves coordinate independence, nor any relation between \(G\) and \(A\) beyond the stated hypotheses.

If \(g>0\), nonnegativity of \(G\) gives \(Q\{G>2g\}\le1/2\) by Markov's inequality, hence \(p_{2g}\ge1/2\). Then \(\sqrt{a/p_{2g}}\le\sqrt{2a}\), and the conditional bound proves the proposed lower bound for \(Z_{2g}\). If \(g=0\), the finite nonnegative function \(G\) has expectation zero. Since \(Q\) is positive at every point of its support, \(G=0\) everywhere on that support. Thus \(p_0=1\), and the same conditional bound proves \(Z_0\ge(\prod_iR_i)e^{-\sqrt a}\). This also implies the weaker displayed bound with factor \(1/2\) and exponent \(-\sqrt{2a}\), so that bound is valid uniformly for \(g\ge0\).

We next construct the packing directly on the original product-table sources. From each nonzero orbit \(\{\mathbf v,-\mathbf v\}\) with \(G(\mathbf v)\le L\), choose the vector whose first nonzero coordinate is positive. This is one choice for the entire vector, with no separate coordinatewise orientation choices. For that representative put \(E_{\mathbf v}=\{\mathbf J+\mathbf v,\mathbf J-\mathbf v\}\) and assign

\[
x_{E_{\mathbf v}}=\min\{w_{\mathbf J+\mathbf v},w_{\mathbf J-\mathbf v}\},
\qquad x_{\{\mathbf J\}}=w_{\mathbf J};
\]

assign zero to all other canonical supports. The preceding gap calculation places every selected pair in \(\mathcal E_{\mathbf J}^{\log}(L)\), and the central singleton is allowed because \(L\ge0\).

Two selected pairs can share a source only if their displacement vectors agree up to a global sign: equality of any two endpoints gives \(\mathbf v=\mathbf u\) or \(\mathbf v=-\mathbf u\). Our representatives therefore give disjoint pair supports. No nonzero pair contains \(\mathbf J\). Each selected source is charged the full mass of just its one component. On a pair that mass is the minimum of its two endpoint capacities and so fits both capacities; on the central singleton it is exactly \(w_{\mathbf J}\). Unselected sources are charged zero. This proves all original capacity constraints with no splitting, duplication, or barycentric-fraction discount.

The endpoint minimum and the cutoff condition are invariant under \(\mathbf v\mapsto-\mathbf v\). The zero displacement contributes exactly \(w_{\mathbf J}\) to \(Z_L\). Consequently the total mass of this feasible packing is

\[
M=w_{\mathbf J}+\sum_{\text{chosen }\mathbf v}\min\{w_{\mathbf J+\mathbf v},w_{\mathbf J-\mathbf v}\}
=w_{\mathbf J}+\frac{Z_L-w_{\mathbf J}}2
=\frac{Z_L+w_{\mathbf J}}2.
\]

The claims about \(P_{\log}\) and \(\mathcal B_{\log}\) follow from their definitions and \(M\ge Z_L/2\).

To prove the quantitative threshold, set \(\ell=1+\log(1/\delta)\) and \(s=m\delta\). These are only scalar abbreviations for the repeated threshold expressions; \(\ell\ge1\). From \(R_i/(W_i/2)=1+2\delta_i\ge1+2\delta\) and

\[
\log(1+2\delta)=\int_0^{2\delta}\frac{dt}{1+t}
\ge\frac{2\delta}{1+2\delta}\ge\delta,
\]

we obtain \(\prod_iR_i/\prod_i(W_i/2)\ge e^s\). The last inequality uses \(\delta\le1/4\); the upper bound \(\delta_i\le2\delta\) is compatible with, but not needed for, this estimate. Combining this gain with the uniformly valid reservoir bound and \(a\le C s\ell^2\) gives

\[
\frac{Z_{2g}}{\prod_i(W_i/2)}
\ge\frac12\exp(s-\sqrt{2a})
\ge\frac12\exp\!\left(s-\sqrt{2Cs}\,\ell\right).
\]

Assume \(s\ge16C\ell^2\). Then \(s\ge16\), and

\[
\sqrt{2Cs}\,\ell\le\sqrt{2Cs\,\frac{s}{16C}}=\frac{s}{\sqrt8}\le\frac{s}2,
\qquad
2g\le2Cs\ell^2\le\frac{s^2}8.
\]

For \(s\ge16\), the cubic term of the exponential series proves

\[
\frac12e^{s/2}\ge\frac{s^3}{96}\ge\frac{s^2}6\ge1+\frac{s^2}8.
\]

Indeed, the middle inequality uses \(s\ge16\), and the last follows from \(s^2/24\ge1\). Thus

\[
\frac{Z_{2g}}{\prod_i(W_i/2)}\ge\frac12e^{s/2}
\ge1+\frac{s^2}8\ge1+2g=1+L.
\]

This proves the claimed threshold with \(K(C)=16C\). Applying the already constructed feasible packing gives \(P_{\log}(\mathbf J,L;w)/(1+L)\ge W/2^{m+1}\). The proof uses the supplied moment hypothesis only for this block and derives neither a one-dimensional price theorem nor a universal all-profile composition.
statement:
Let \(m\ge1\) be an integer. For \(1\le i\le m\), let \(w^i=(w^i_k)_{k\in\mathbb Z}\) be a nonzero, nonnegative, finitely supported complete one-dimensional log-concave profile: it has a finite-valued log-concave extension \(f_i:\mathbb R\to[0,\infty)\) agreeing with every table entry, including every zero. Put \(D_i=\{k:w^i_k>0\}\), \(W_i=\sum_{k\in D_i}w^i_k\), and \(w^i_{\max}=\max_{k\in D_i}w^i_k\). Use the canonical potential \(\phi_i(k)=\log(w^i_{\max}/w^i_k)\) for \(k\in D_i\), and choose any integer center \(J_i\in D_i\). These are the one-dimensional specialization of the table, total-weight, potential, and center conventions of accepted fact `488f0a583886b5fc`. All logarithms are natural.

Define the finite symmetric displacement support \(\mathcal U_{J_i}=\{v\in\mathbb Z:J_i+v,J_i-v\in D_i\}\) and the reflected reservoir and law by

\[
\begin{aligned}
R_i&=\sum_{v\in\mathcal U_{J_i}}\sqrt{w^i_{J_i+v}w^i_{J_i-v}},
&Q_i(v)&=\frac{\sqrt{w^i_{J_i+v}w^i_{J_i-v}}}{R_i},\\
G_i(v)&=\frac{\phi_i(J_i+v)+\phi_i(J_i-v)}2-\phi_i(J_i),
&A_i(v)&=\frac{\phi_i(J_i+v)-\phi_i(J_i-v)}2.
\end{aligned}
\]

Here \(R_i>0\); \(Q_i\) is a probability law on \(\mathcal U_{J_i}\), \(G_i\) is even and nonnegative, and \(A_i\) is odd. Set \(g=\sum_i\mathbb E_{Q_i}G_i\ge0\) and \(a=\sum_i\mathbb E_{Q_i}A_i^2<\infty\).

Form only this finite block table in integer dimension \(m\):

\[
\begin{aligned}
w_{\mathbf I}&=\prod_{i=1}^m w^i_{I_i},
&D&=\prod_{i=1}^m D_i,
&W&=\prod_{i=1}^m W_i,\\
\mathbf J&=(J_1,\ldots,J_m),
&w_{\max}&=\prod_{i=1}^m w^i_{\max},
&\phi_{\mathbf I}&=\log\frac{w_{\max}}{w_{\mathbf I}}=\sum_{i=1}^m\phi_i(I_i)\quad(\mathbf I\in D).
\end{aligned}
\]

Retain the canonical definitions of `488f0a583886b5fc`: \(\mathcal E_{\mathbf J}\) consists of the nonempty affinely independent \(E\subseteq D\) with \(\mathbf J\in\operatorname{relint}\operatorname{conv}E\), with their unique positive barycentric coefficients \(\lambda_{E,\mathbf I}\). Their gap is \(G_E=\sum_{\mathbf I\in E}\lambda_{E,\mathbf I}\phi_{\mathbf I}-\phi_{\mathbf J}\). For \(L\ge0\),

\[
\begin{aligned}
P_{\log}(\mathbf J,L;w)
&=\max\left\{\sum_{\substack{E\in\mathcal E_{\mathbf J}\\G_E\le L}}x_E:
x_E\ge0,\quad
\sum_{\substack{E\in\mathcal E_{\mathbf J}\\G_E\le L,\ \mathbf I\in E}}x_E\le w_{\mathbf I}
\quad(\mathbf I\in D)\right\},\\
\mathcal B_{\log}(w)
&=\max_{\mathbf J'\in D,\ L'\ge0}\frac{P_{\log}(\mathbf J',L';w)}{1+L'}.
\end{aligned}
\]

Thus each source in a component is charged its full component mass, not its barycentric fraction, and all components share the original capacities \(w_{\mathbf I}\).

Let \(Q=\bigotimes_{i=1}^m Q_i\) on \(\mathcal U_{\mathbf J}=\prod_i\mathcal U_{J_i}\). Write \(G(\mathbf v)=\sum_iG_i(v_i)\) and \(A(\mathbf v)=\sum_iA_i(v_i)\); for \(\mathbf v\ne\mathbf0\), \(G(\mathbf v)\) is precisely the canonical gap of the pair \(\{\mathbf J+\mathbf v,\mathbf J-\mathbf v\}\). Define the oriented stock, including both orientations and the zero displacement, by

\[
Z_L=\sum_{\substack{\mathbf v\in\mathcal U_{\mathbf J}\\G(\mathbf v)\le L}}
\min\{w_{\mathbf J+\mathbf v},w_{\mathbf J-\mathbf v}\},
\qquad p_L=Q\{G\le L\}.
\]

For every \(L\ge0\), \(p_L>0\), and the exact stock identity and finite-probability lower bound are

\[
Z_L=\left(\prod_iR_i\right)\mathbb E_Q\!\left[e^{-|A|}\mathbf1_{\{G\le L\}}\right]
\ge\left(\prod_iR_i\right)p_L\exp\!\left(-\sqrt{\frac a{p_L}}\right).
\]

In particular, with the canonical gap cutoff \(L=2g\),

\[
Z_{2g}\ge\frac12\left(\prod_iR_i\right)e^{-\sqrt{2a}}.
\]

If \(g=0\), the cutoff is \(L=0\), \(p_0=1\), and the stronger bound \(Z_0\ge(\prod_iR_i)e^{-\sqrt a}\) holds. The finite-probability inequality uses only symmetry of the independent laws, oddness of the imbalance functions, nonnegativity of the gap functions, and the displayed moment statistics.

For every \(L\ge0\), there is a feasible canonical packing using the central singleton and one representative of each eligible orbit \(\{\mathbf v,-\mathbf v\}\) of nonzero displacements. If \(M\) denotes its total component mass, then

\[
M=\frac{Z_L+w_{\mathbf J}}2\ge\frac{Z_L}2,
\qquad P_{\log}(\mathbf J,L;w)\ge M,
\qquad \mathcal B_{\log}(w)\ge\frac{Z_L}{2(1+L)}.
\]

Each original product-table site occurs in at most one selected component and is charged that component's full mass. No geometric mean is used as a legal capacity, and orientation is selected once globally, not separately in each coordinate.

Finally, fix any \(C\ge1\) and \(0<\delta\le1/4\). Suppose

\[
\delta_i:=\frac{R_i}{W_i}-\frac12\in[\delta,2\delta]\quad(1\le i\le m),
\qquad a+g\le C m\delta\bigl(1+\log(1/\delta)\bigr)^2.
\]

The sufficient threshold \(m\delta\ge K(C)(1+\log(1/\delta))^2\), with \(K(C)=16C\), implies, at \(L=2g\),

\[
Z_L\ge(1+L)\prod_{i=1}^m\frac{W_i}2
=(1+L)\frac W{2^m},
\qquad
\frac{P_{\log}(\mathbf J,L;w)}{1+L}\ge\frac W{2^{m+1}}.
\]

This is a conditional finite-block conclusion; it asserts no price bound guaranteeing its moment hypotheses for arbitrary profiles.
